utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We resume with the cross-examination of this witness, which was suspended on Friday afternoon. Mr. Witness, I would remind you that you're still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Witness. Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm going to read a provision of the Law on General People's Defence. We spoke a little bit about resubordination, and we spent a little bit of time on that. And the law regulates that, and it defines it much more succinctly. So Article 104 states: "In war during immediate danger of war or imminent danger of war, and in other extraordinary circumstances, the police can be used also to execute combat assignments of the armed forces pursuant to the law."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we do not have the original text in front us.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: "During the time it is executing combat tasks" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour? It's very brief. It's a very brief provision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 104 of the Law on General People's Defence. I'm only going to read it. May I continue with paragraph 2: "During the time that they're executing combat assignments of the armed forces, the police is resubordinated to the authorised senior officer who is conducting the combat actions."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, were you thinking about this provision when we were talking about resubordination? You're probably familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us just remind ourselves. You said that you were at the -- that you transferred to the National Defence Secretariat from the police in March. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late March and early April 1992, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And you're aware of this provision, or you're familiar with this provision of the law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to say -- to put it -- actually, I didn't read that law, but I understood the whole story basically from attending the police academy before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you understood the gist of what we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now that we're talking about the resubordination provision, I'm going to describe a hypothetical situation to you now. You would agree with me, would you not --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have turned the microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: In such a situation, if the police officer or the unit that is resubordinated to the military police commits a serious crime or a war crime, according to what we have established so far they would be placed under the jurisdiction of the military judicial organs, the military investigative judge, the military prosecutor, and the military court. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, this law and some other regulations that go with it provide for the obligation of drafting war plans and the formation or the establishment of War Staffs, whereby I'm not thinking of the military pyramid from the supreme commander, the Supreme Staff, the armed forces, and so on and so forth. I'm not thinking about the armed component of the armed forces because they had their own plans and their own staffs. I am thinking of all the other subjects. You are aware that all -- everyone had to have these plans, even the economic subjects, companies, schools, municipalities. I cannot be sure, but I think this even applied to local communes. Do you remember that obligation to make plans?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And the organ of internal affairs was also subject to that obligation, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, these plans do not resemble military plans of the army. They're not plans to execute combat actions, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to dwell a little bit on what is of interest to us, and that is the police. We have already established that a certain proportion of the police could, according to an order by the supreme commander, be engaged in the armed forces, and that then places them outside of the jurisdiction of the police, placing them under the armed forces. However, the rest of the police force in war has to continue to perform its regular tasks. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that at any given time they are also essentially subject or subordinate to the supreme military command structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with you that that is once the command decides to place them under their jurisdiction, but some of them have to deal with their regular assignments, with dealing with criminals, and so on. No region can be left without the activities of the police.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot be sure, but I think in the case of imminent danger of war the police or the militia would be engaged at the front or on their own regular assignments, but they would still be subject to decisions adopted by the military command, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you believe that even the sector of the police that was not directly engaged in combat actions are still subordinated to the military command during wartime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during wartime, because at any point they can tell them --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness and Mr. Cvijetic, sorry, the interpreters did not get the last answer by the witness. So if he could please repeat it so that we can hear what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness would need to repeat his answer. I don't need to repeat my question. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Why don't you just repeat it just to be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: From what I understood you to say, you think that the rest of the police was also subject to military command and would be subordinate to the military command, because at any point in time they could be engaged in action. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Witness, in closing I would like to read another portion from a law. You said that you completed the military academy at the -- the police academy at the secondary level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I completed the cadet school, the secondary level of military academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So practically your profession is a policeman; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And you are -- you were trained as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: While you were employed, did you enjoy the status of an authorised person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the police, with the police, yes; but when I was transferred to the Secretariat for the National Defence, then I ceased to be an authorised person.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. I would like to read now a -- an excerpt from a law, and I would just like to check with you whether you are aware of it. It reads as follows: "I declare that I will carry out" -- "discharge my duties as a authorised person in a responsible and ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us what you're reading please, article, law?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. This is a provision from the law on the interior, the provision number 14 of the Law on the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina which was in force while the gentleman was undergoing training for police work. May I -- may I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So I have to repeat this. "I declare that I will carry out the duties as an authorised person in a conscientious and responsible manner; that I will abide by the laws and the constitution; and that I will protect the constitutional order, laws, rights, liberties, and security of the working people and citizens to the best of my abilities; and that I will carry out these and other responsibilities as an authorised person in a -- even in the event where such duties and tasks may endanger my life." Do you know what I've read from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this is a -- an oath of office that we all had to -- to take before we started our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but under the law I believe that was called a solemn oath.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible, but I can't really recall right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me remind you. That's what it says. It says: "The text of the solemn oath reads as follows ..." And then comes what I've just read. Well, let me ask you then. Did you take this solemn oath?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I would now like to go back briefly to those plans that all the other subjects have to prepare. In practice these plans are referred to as war plans. Would it be more appropriate to use the term "plans on the organisation and manner of operation of that particular subject under wartime conditions"? Would that explain more precisely what exactly this law referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. But before I sit down, I would like to thank the witness for his very fair and honest replies. I believe that up until this moment you have fully abided by the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of this trial. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Dragan Krgovic, and I will put some questions on behalf of the Defence for Stojan Zupljanin that relate to your testimony a few days ago. Witness, in response to a question by the Prosecution and my colleague Cvijetic, you talked about the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina operated at the time in question, and my questions will relate precisely to those areas and responsibilities and work of some of the organs of the MUP. Are you familiar with the fact that under the old law there was especially -- a special service of state security within the structure of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this was a separate organisational unit which had special rules of service; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And although at times it would share the premises with the Public Security Service, it was actually in charge of the special area of responsibility which was the state security, and it did not get involved in the public security aspects of work; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And they had special premises where other members of the police could not -- or had no access without permission or authorisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, they had a separate chain of command and practically they were a service within a service; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question by the Prosecution, you said that you were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's request: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I have to repeat my question because it didn't enter into the transcript. So you were arrested by some military persons, but you're not sure whether these were reserve policemen or regular police -- or regular army personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My question referred to military personnel, and what you just said referred to military personnel; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, reserve military personnel, but whether they were regular soldiers or not, I don't know, but they did wear army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And after this you were questioned by members of the state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was brought to the security services centre, the first contact I had was with a member of the state security whom I knew before. I knew that he worked at this service, in this service. And the second contact that I had was with an inspector, but whether he was a member of the regular police or state security, I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you provided or made any statement to these individuals who questioned you? Did you sign any statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first -- on that first occasion the gentleman who was a member of the state security offered that I sign a statement which said that I was arrested because I was allegedly an organiser of an armed rebellion, and I refused to sign this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will get back to this question on how they treated you, but my general question, because you were an inspector, a crime inspector, the standard procedure in your work, crime inspector, would be to take a statement from a witness, to collect evidence, and prepare a criminal report which would then be forwarded to the authorised prosecutor; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Following this, the prosecutor would decide whether there was official grounds to undertake an investigation, and you as a policeman had no further connections with the proceedings that were -- that he would instigate, that he would start; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And whatever happened with the arrested individuals was really not within your jurisdiction any more; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 2D06-90097 -- 2D60-097 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will show you a copy of one of the statements that you gave to the State Security Service, the Banja Luka section. Please read it carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, do you know if there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please keep this document under seal. It is not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know if there is an English translation of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. It's on the screen. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, could you check whether your signature is on this page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And we can see your signature on each and every one of these pages, at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the questions that were put to you when you take a look at this statement? Does it reflect what you said on this occasion while you were questioned by the state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the time elapsed, I cannot really vouch that everything was written down as I said it, but for the most part all of it is in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, more or less all the topics that you discussed are in there; correct? I just need you to confirm whether, generally speaking, this is what you said. Whether this content is or reflects what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 2D06 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the second part of the number of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, second one or previous one?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note the counsel is switching his microphone on and off, and we could not hear the entire number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could you please do it once again because the microphone was switched on and off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have 060097. That was the earlier exhibit. Could we please admit it into evidence, and the witness confirmed that this was in fact his document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose it's being admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. It will be Exhibit 2D2 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 060103, please. And if I can, with the assistance of the Usher, could a copy of this document be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just confirm it's not actually going out over the monitors. I just wanted to check. That's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is not being broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you have -- did you have an opportunity to see this now? Could you check that your signature is on this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my signature, but I have not seen this before except at the time perhaps when it was noted down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But it more or less reflects what you talked about with the State Security Service inspectors when you talked with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes, because I have nothing to hide. Not then, so I spoke openly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And they mostly questioned you about what you knew about the arming of the Muslim and the Croatian people, about meetings with certain people, and whether you yourself had any weapons. These were more or less the topics of the conversation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: They also asked you to explain the origin of the automatic rifle and pistol found in your house, and you gave the explanation as it is stated in this statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have an exhibit number for this exhibit, please, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D3 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see that there is another statement coming now, and I would like to ask you if you would be good enough to explain to us what it is exactly that you wish the Court to extract from these statements other than the fact, of course, that he was questioned by the state security in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm trying to demonstrate or show the Chamber that the procedure and the authorisation, what they are of those people who conducted the procedure against this witness, from the taking of the statement, to the criminal charges, to the arrest of the witness, and so on and so forth, and under whose jurisdiction he stayed in prison. Also who is responsible for the abuse of this witness while he was in prison. This whole line of questioning will be based on a series of documents showing who was in charge of him, who was questioning him, who kept him in detention, and who beat him, whereby I wish to demonstrate that this had nothing to do with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is excellent information. Thank you very much. And please help the Court to get to this point so that we can understand the evidence that you bring.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I have another statement here that you provided to the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could witness look at 2D06-0109, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just going to show you the statement. I'm not going to be dealing with it in detail. Could you just confirm whether it is your signature, whether you gave this statement, and if you recall the conversation on which the statement was based?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I could save the Usher some time. I don't need to be shown statements in B/C/S, which I can't read, and ask if I object to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you had the opportunity to check whether this is your signature on the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And just as in the previous statement, does it more or less reflect the conversation that you had with the members of the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please be given an exhibit number for this document, also under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D3 under seal, Your Honours. Apologies, Exhibit 2D4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just now I asked you about the procedure when an authorised employee of the police completes the compilation of documents and the interviews and then he submits criminal charges. Did you have the opportunity to see the criminal charges submitted against you together with the accompanying documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal charges as such without the accompanying documents I did see for the first and last time when I was brought before the military prosecutor or the judge. I'm not sure which.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D00-4474. [In English] Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, if I may. You make a difference between -- you make a difference between State Security Service and Public Security Service. Now, I have the document. You ask questions about -- to the witness, and you say this is State Security Service. What is -- what is indicated that it is state and not public?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: How can I see that it is state and not public? I see -- in the translation I see Security Service Centre. I don't see specified that it is state or public, but perhaps I'm missing something here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Underneath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Underneath? I don't have the underneath.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. It says: "Security Services Centre Banja Luka." And then it says: "SNB."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: SNB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. National Security Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 3 of this document just to see -- I think you are the last person on that list. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to note that this is the first time that I am seeing these criminal charges in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the attachments carefully. These are statements of persons who are referred to in the criminal charges and provided as attachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we move into private session for a moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We're now in open session, so please be careful, and I will, too, in my questions, not to mention any fact that might point to your identity, just as a reminder. Now, once a criminal report was submitted, there would be a decision made on conducting an investigation and on arrest on remand. Is that how it worked? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the normal circumstances that would be the regular procedure. However, I and these two other individuals were put in prison without receiving any decision or anything of that sort, and it was only a month later that we received the first paper that we could read and see what it was that we were charged with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And before that you said that you had refused to sign a statement in -- at the station because you felt that you were not responsible for what was being charged against you. Do you recall that, saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The decision of -- by the Public Security Service to put you under arrest, that is what -- that is the type of decision I was referring to, and you were not given this decision to sign?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say "public security," "state security."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was an A4 sheet of paper with two or three sentences on it, a very brief text, and I refused to sign that. And as for this, this is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the paper that you refused to sign stated that you were put under arrest; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about -- it was about something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And following this, you received from a court -- you received a court decision putting you under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 2D05-0037. Just a moment. Perhaps I can provide a copy, but I think it is easier to read off the monitor. 2D0300 --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 00 what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We can see here that you and the other two colleagues that were with you were placed under arrest by the lower court in the city or town where you were arrested.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You submitted a complaint -- or, rather, an appeal against this ruling. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will show that document a little later, but before that, could we admit this document into evidence under seal as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D5 -- 2D6 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 2D03-0041, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision whereby your appeal is rejected. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After this, you were transferred to a military prison, you testified before this Court. In other words, you were transferred from a civilian to a military prison. And I would now like to show you a document which explains why that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the meantime, could we show the witness 2D03-00345.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Counsel, before you move on, are you exhibited this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D7 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision where the lower court in the town where you were arrested proclaimed itself -- proclaimed that it did not have jurisdiction over this matter, and it forwarded this to the Banja Luka court. Is this -- does this actually correspond to your transfer from the civilian to the military prison, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really claim with certainty that this happened at about the same time on that particular date, but I believe that this was at the time when we were in prison. We spent some month or month and a half in prison. And then in June we were in a different prison. So this could be a document relating to that, but I'm not absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Following this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we admit this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D8 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown 2D03-0050.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from a higher court where, prior to this case being forwarded to the military court, you are -- your arrest is being extended. Do you agree with me? Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit this document into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D9 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour. Maybe -- maybe I'm wrong, but there is some -- mistake in exhibit numbers. I think the previous one with last two digits 0045 should be 2D7, and that one 2D8, because now we are running to the other number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pantelic. The Registry will check and make the necessary adjustments. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could a document be shown, 2D03-0059. Could the witness be shown the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It is rather illegible. These are notes from your interview before the military prosecutor. Could you just briefly look at the second page and tell us whether this reflects your interview, the content of your interview with the military prosecutor. As far as I could see, it is more or less consistent with the previous statements. Please take a look at the fifth paragraph from the top where your description of the inspections of the shelters exactly reflects your words here before this Trial Chamber. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the copy is really difficult to read. I'm unable to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me read it. It says here: "Regarding shelters, I state that I did not visit any kind of shelters in the area of other villages."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm reminding counsel that we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will give you a copy of this document, but I can tell you that what is stated therein more or less it corresponds to what you've already mentioned in the other statements. But perhaps you can take a look at this copy just to confirm. More or less, this is what you said to the investigating judge; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D10 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned during your testimony on Friday that you were also assigned a counsel ex officio. Do you remember that you said this on Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, but I didn't -- I wasn't given an opportunity to correct myself. The counsel who was assigned to me, it's possible that he was assigned ex officio, but this was a man that I knew from before. So whether he was an assigned counsel or whether I actually sought him, I'm not really sure anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 2D03-0053, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is your appeal from the decision on remand in custody that your counsel actually filed with the court, and he asked that the -- that the proceedings against you be annulled and that you be released. So this is the content of this appeal, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D11 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that when you went on that exchange that you received a decision issued by the military court that the prosecutor had withdrawn a criminal complaint against you and that it was ordered that you be released from remand. Do you recall -- from remand and custody. Do you recall that you said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness 2D03-0056, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly what we were talking about. It says here that you were no longer to be held in custody, you and the others, because the prosecutor was not going to pursue the criminal report. Also, appeal was not permitted because the parties had waived their right to it. You said last time when you testified that you had not waived that right. Is that what you meant when you said -- did you mean to say that you did not waive your right to appeal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did comment on that in the sense that this was written as a kind of legal remedy, but I didn't have the opportunity to appeal at all. I received a blank A4 piece of paper then, which I also had to sign. I signed the blank piece of paper. I don't know what was written on that paper later. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But basically this decision is in your favour. You didn't have a lawyer. All charges against you were rejected, so any lawyer would waive the right to appeal for his client because this is something that would be beneficial to his client. Would you not agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, when is the time for the break? Because I have 15 minutes more. Should I go now or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have seven minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In short, what I wanted to show with these documents, you were suspected of taking part in armed rebellion, that you had weapons. You provided statements. Some of the witnesses provided statements that were not in your favour. You went through the entire procedure from the criminal report to being acquitted. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went through the entire procedure, as you put it, but the mistreatment, the beatings, that is not a procedure that is provided for under any regulations. And if I may say, at the time there was a sort of quasi-state in power, and the procedure resembled that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not talking about what actually happened. I am just saying that the procedures conducted against were you conducted in accordance with the procedure that was in force at the time without referring to the beatings, the abuse, and what happened with you while you were in prison, or without saying that that was legal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the regulations in force at the time, the jurisdiction over those detained in the district prison was under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Justice or the court police or a special district prison. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really comment on that. I'm no longer sure about that or whose jurisdiction that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you were serving the jurisdiction over those who the court placed under custody, was under the jurisdiction of the court or the military prosecutor or the district prosecutor under whose' jurisdiction the court would place them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you were under the jurisdiction the military court, so this dual jurisdiction would then be something that was under the military organs. It was under military jurisdiction, and that's who had jurisdiction over you up until the time you were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As I understand it, only from -- if this is true, only from the 1st of October. Up till then it was the civilian authorities that had jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. According to the documents that counsel just produced, on the 1st of October the lower court, whoever that may have been, refused jurisdiction and said it would be transmitted to the military court. So certainly until the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the gist of my question. I can see that perhaps I formulated it clumsily or perhaps the interpretation was a little bit problematic, but in any case, that was the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you were questioned by the investigative judge or by members of the State Security Service, were you asked about your affiliation to or with HVO units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you were asked about the existence of organised groups of the Muslim Croatian ethnicity and their weaponry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were questions to that effect, but from what I knew there was no organised form of resistance. I said what I knew, that there weren't such groups. And it's true that there weren't such groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's a convenient time for the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, before I continue, I asked you about an abbreviation, HVO. We know what I meant. But for the Trial Chamber, can you please explain what that abbreviation means. It means the Croatian Defence Council, I will say, and it was a armed force of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina at a certain period in time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please -- Your Honours, I apologise. I forgot to ask for the previous document to be admitted. It is this decision on suspending the proceedings against the witness, and that is number -- just one moment. 2D00-056.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It's now admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So will become Exhibit 2D12 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 2D05-0016.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we don't have an English translation for this document, but if you agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We do. We supplied an English translation of the header.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we're talking about a different document. I'm talking about the second -- oh, we have it for this one as well. Your Honours, I have photocopies of the heading for the Trial Chamber. The rest of the document are just names. This is a document of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, of the Ministry of Defence. It's a secret, military secret, classified as a military secret, and it is the list of persons registered at the defence office. Could the witness please be shown the page of the document marked ERN 071-4627.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0710-4626.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at line marked third from the bottom on this document. I'm not going to state the number. 529. This first column is your name there and the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And next to that we see your personal ID number with your date and year of birth in the first part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the next column we see the time of service in the units, from the 18th of September, 1991, until the 11th of June, 1992. Register number 3215/60; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you help us and explain -- first of all, did you have the opportunity to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not before the proofing, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It states here on this document - I'm not saying that that is a fact - that you were a member of the HVO from this date, the 11th of September, 1999, up until the time you were arrested, if I understand this document correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The translation comes up as the 11th of September, 1999, which can't be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation of how your name happens to be on this list and that you were engaged in the HVO forces for this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This period that is referred to here in 1991 until June 1992, I don't know, because I could not have been a member of those units because I was still working in the police until the -- until late March 1992. And the second date that is mentioned here, I assume that -- and in general about this list, it probably included all persons who in one way or another were victims of these unfortunate events, and it was evidently a political decision at some higher level that really is not accessible to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 2D05-0013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before you move on, is there any application that you have to make in respect of this document that was last shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when I show the witness the second document, I will show their connection, and then I will seek for admittance of both. Because what he was talking about now was actually what I'm going to show in the second document. So I just want to make sure there is no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, under 21 here we can see your name. And again we see the personal identification number. And I assume that this is you, in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We can see here where it says: "In captivity as of 11th June, 1992." And there's also -- this, in fact, is a list of disabled veterans of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that this was probably compiled for the benefit of those people who were victims, and I suppose you were referring to this document, because this document really relates to individuals who are to be reimbursed for their disability and the other document was just a list, but I assume that these two documents, in fact, go hand in hand, and that they are proof for some claims that you may have; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both of these documents are -- they're inseparable, in fact. They go together, but obviously up until the HVO was established as mentioned, and I don't know exactly when and under whose instructions, but when this conflict broke out, I'm pretty certain that this did not exist. And as far as I know, they did not have this information at their disposal. But whether this -- these lists were compiled while I was in custody, I don't know. And I believe that they were compiled really in order to enable the individuals who were victims of this conflict to regulate their status.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was my conclusion, too, and that is why I linked up these two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please admit both of these documents, under seal, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Tendered, admitted, and marked with the next number in the series.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Both documents will become Exhibit 2D13 and 2D14. Both will be under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you, sir. Your Honours, my cross-examination is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there will be. One thing I don't think we've been told so far, does re-examination count as far as the hours allocated? I see Judge Harhoff nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Was I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We'll get back to you. My immediate response is, Yes, of course it is included. But I'm not sure, and we're having the Legal Officer check for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I assure the Legal Officer and save some time. You never mentioned re-examination, but I'm -- I'll continue, and we'll see how -- how we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked on Friday, I believe, about something to do about Crisis Staffs, and you explained how you'd seen a document in a previous trial in relation to that. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before you saw that document in the previous trials, were you aware of Crisis Staffs and how they operated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned of their existence, the existence of the Crisis Staff, from the operative, the inspector who was interviewing me when I was arrested. And as for the role and function of that Crisis Staff, at the time I didn't know anything about it; but after, I learned something about it after I was released.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next, you were asked this afternoon about your understanding of how the police and the military interacted in times of war. Do you remember those questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you had part of the Law on All People's Defence read to you this afternoon. Have you ever read the Law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this afternoon was the first time that you had heard that particular article before; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You also explain that your understanding of the role of the police was that in all matters, including civilian law enforcement, they were subject to military authority if there was a time of war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So in other words, your understanding is that it would be the local military officer, the senior military officer, who would be in charge of the police in all matters in a time of war. Is that what you're saying? Not just if the police were in combat units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the police had their own commander who was subordinate to the military commander, who could then issue any type of assignment to him and he would have to obey.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So I just want to -- so we all get what your understanding is, it's your understanding that, for example, Stojan Zupljanin would have been subordinate to General Momir Talic in respect of all matters to do with the police and not subordinate to Mico Stanisic. Is that what you're saying your understanding is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I assume that no order, even if it came from a military -- from the military, could be issued without the minister of the interior or without going through the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say, "I assume." Is all of what you've been saying an assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These -- this is the knowledge that I have about the chain of command in the -- in war time or imminent threat of war, and that is how it worked while I was arrested. But from that moment onward, I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. During your service as a police officer in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that when the witness said that this order could not go unnoticed by the minister of the interior or without his consent, but it would have to be obeyed in any case. Am I correct in saying that, Witness? [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'm now -- that's the trouble. I'm now confused as to whether the intervention is because the translation of the witness's answer was wrong or whether Mr. Cvijetic is trying to ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation was incomplete of the witness's words. This portion was missing. But the portion saying that in any case, that order would have to be implemented, so that portion was not interpreted. And that was really the gist of my intervention.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think, just to be clear, we'd better go back over this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you whether Stojan Zupljanin would have been subordinate to General Talic in respect of all matters to do with the police and not subordinate to Mico Stanisic, and I asked you what your understanding was. Can you tell us again what your reply would be? I think that's the best way of sorting this out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that an army general would not address directly, as far as I understand it, anyone from the chain of command. And the way I understood the chain of command in the former state, he would not really address in any way the commander of the CSB but, rather, would go through the minister if an assignment had to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I was just about to ask you whether during your period of service in the police in the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia you had operated in a time of war ever or imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ST-27 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally, you've just been asked a number of questions about the proceedings that were taken against you in court. First of all, can we just look at the context again of those statements that you made, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was trying to think whether we should go into private session, and I think we should, if you don't mind, for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And while we go into private session, we have checked through our Legal Officer what the position is for time for re-examination, and the answer is that it is not part of the time set aside for your examination-in-chief. The redirect forms part of the remaining 20 per cent that are added for questions from the Judges, procedural matters, and re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We return to private session for questions by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the break I got the instruction of my client, Mr. Zupljanin, to address this witness. [Interpretation] I'm now going to speak in the language you understand. Mr. Zupljanin would like to express his regret for everything that you had experienced during the period you described in front of this Trial Chamber. He found out about it by reading statements and listening to what you have said. And in view of the fact that you spent (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'd better have that very last bit redacted from the public transcript. That is to say, from line -- from page 45, lines 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner. So you're now released, and we wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know whether the shutters are going to go up or down, but, Your Honours, can I mention a couple of matters before Mr. Di Fazio calls the next witness. For the purposes of the transcript, Mr. Di Fazio has come into court. Really, procedural matters. The first is this: We're actually moving from Kotor Varos into Sanski Most, and you may have gathered --

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Should we be in open session?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Oh, we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's just that the shutters are down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, correct me if I'm wrong, but you are -- you just indicated who would be leading the next witness, and I seem to recall that I neglected this morning, notwithstanding what I indicated last week I would do after each resumption, to take the appearances afresh. So perhaps I'd better do that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's pretty clear, but, Your Honour, the appearances for the Prosecution for the first witness today were myself, Joanna Korner, assisted by the case manager Jasmina Bosnjakovic, and Mr. Di Fazio has just arrived in court. So that's the Prosecution for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am co-counsel in Mr. Mico Stanisic's Defence, and I conducted the cross-examination today. I am accompanied by Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, and our legal assistant right now Ms. Tatjana Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, Brent Hicks, and Eric Tully. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So now we're back on course. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just explain. The evidence on Kotor Varos is not actually complete, and I'm afraid we're not calling the evidence in any particularly logical fashion because of the problems with witnesses who we are banned from calling until one month afterwards. That's a problem which I'm afraid has hit us again. In respect of the witness who was due to come on Friday -- sorry. Yes, probably Friday. A review of the searches that were done on him revealed that there had been a nine-page statement made to the Bosnians which has just turned up and which is not translated into English. That puts him out of court, as it were, in light of Your Honours' ruling. The way we see the week proceeding is as follows: There is the witness that Mr. Di Fazio will call now who is 92 ter and who Mr. Di Fazio tells me will take about 20 minutes in chief, as per the instructions. The estimate for cross-examination from each team has been, I think, 30 -- sorry, no. What number's that? Forty-five minutes from the Zupljanin team, and 30 minutes from the Stanisic team. There is another witness tomorrow. The length of cross-examination is a bit longer for the two of them, and I think examination-in-chief, Ms. Pidwell's going to ask if she's can have a little bit long with this particular witness. The witness after that is going to be a lengthy witness. Your Honour will recall Witness 181 this is, that a witness summons was issued for him. There was a problem with his visa, so he's not getting here till tonight. He's then going to review his interviews and the documents. And the Defence have told us today that they would like to interview him as well, which, of course, is their right. But that means that we can't start him until, effectively, Wednesday. Which in any event, I think, would be the case because of the delay in him getting his visa, even if the Defence didn't want to talk to him. He's likely to -- he will certainly take all of Wednesday, for the most part in chief; and judging by the estimates for cross-examinations, Thursday. But we don't have the witness that we wanted to, or we've just stopped the witness coming because of the statement, and also it transpires that although he's -- his English statement was disclosed some time ago, way back in June, for some unknown reason it's fallen through the cracks again. We didn't translate it into the language of the accused. We therefore inform -- we informed the Defence last week that if we were starting to run out of witnesses, which we might because the videolink is set for Tuesday on the basis of this particular witness, we were proposing to call Dorothea Hanson to deal with Crisis Staffs. Now, the Defence were told this last week, but I think it's caused some consternation that we're proposing to put this witness in. But that's the only way that we can, at the moment, fill the required time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are you asking that Ms. Hanson be called to testify on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we're hoping to do, and I can see Mr. Pantelic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like to underline that we are not in a state of consternation, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am so sorry. I shouldn't have used that expression. But that's the situation, Your Honours. It's either effectively Ms. Hanson or nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And for how long will the examination-in-chief of Ms. Hanson last?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, we gave the lawyer a shock, too, who was going to call her, when we said we would do it, so we're checking. I would have thought the standard for an expert, I think you allowed us an hour. Yes. I think it's unlikely to be longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And so -- and what is the position of the Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, it's not so much consternation as objection to calling Dorothea Hanson Friday. We are not in a position to be ready for an expert on such short notice. Things have changed. We were advised on the 2nd that Hanson and someone else may be interspersed, but clearly the assumption there, I think, is that if we ran out of witnesses during the course of October, then Hanson and the other person would come in. But we're not prepared today, learning today, to be able to cross-examine an expert who has a very large and important report and whose subject matter is very important to the Defence. So your order to grant us relief that precludes the Friday's witness, because of late disclosure after the 31st of July, we say is there to protect us. Now, we shouldn't be put in a position where we're granted relief on the one hand because of late disclosure after 31st July, and then be told on Monday that the - did I mention the name? - the Crisis Staff expert is coming. We're not prepared for that. We cannot be prepared to adequately cross-examine this witness. We would need more lead time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, the Zupljanin Defence is standing along these lines of Mr. O'Sullivan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you see, this is -- I'm sorry. I didn't realise you were discussing matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, we may have this in our papers, but could you remind us as to who you have scheduled for Monday? Your videolink witness is Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Monday would be --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Monday would have been the witness -- I've forgotten his number. In fact, I'm reminded, we've got one other witness before -- or, sorry, after Witness 181 and that's ST-13. I've forgotten about ST-13; a small witness. We were going to have the witness that, as a result of checking the searches, we can't call because there is an extra statement. I mean -- and in fact, we've stopped the witness now. But the realistic thing is, Your Honours, is the Defence could quite easily read this statement themselves and see that it doesn't -- we've had it read -- it doesn't really add anything at all. But, Your Honours, having said, unless the Defence agree we can't call them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- the reason for my question about Monday was that when next -- assuming that the Chamber's inclined to agree with the difficulties that -- with the position taken by the Defence in terms of your proposed witness for Friday, when next would she be available?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, that witness. No, no. She's here. There's no problem. She can give evidence any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: She's a proper fill in, because we can get hold of her at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the logical question that flows from that to the Defence is: If not Friday, when? This witness is available at any time according to Ms. Korner. As I said, assuming we agree with you that Friday is a surprise to you and you shouldn't be expected to meet it, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, we would just like to have more notice than four days. I mean -- and we acknowledge that the Prosecution has been courteous enough to give us names for the whole month of October, and it's a question of balance. I can't say it's more than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We understand that, Mr. O'Sullivan. I was simply trying to -- to avoid gaps. If this is a witness who is basically available any time, to avoid a recurrence of your being caught by surprise at four days' notice, now that you are on notice, when -- would you wish to volunteer to the Prosecution when would be appropriate to call her? But that's an aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes. It was -- the circumstances of the late discovery by the Prosecution that has affected Friday's witness, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, we could -- one of the ways we could deal with this is if my learned friends consider that Monday's sufficient notice, she could be dealt with on Monday in chief. We could do the videolink witness on Tuesday, and we anticipate Wednesday, and then return for her to cross-examination. The one thing we don't want is for her to -- her cross-examination to be delayed for a long time, because she's working on other trials and she needs to be able to talk to other members of the office. Alternatively, we could use one of the days, I suppose, to sort out the rest of the outstanding motions. But I mean, that's -- I'm sorry. And I appreciate that we take responsibility for the fact that this particular statement slipped through the net, and I'm afraid it's teething problems at the beginning of a case, but that's where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, do I understand it well that if ST-177 falls out, you don't have a witness on Monday either?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because 177 would have taken up Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the matter, what to do, and we are also concerned about the loss of time, because every time we lose out a witness the ending of the Prosecution's case is being pushed further out in the end, so our proposal is that you call Ms. Hanson for examination-in-chief on Friday, and you spend that one hour with her and then we adjourn. And we would then ask the Defence teams to be ready to begin their cross-examination on Monday and complete on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That should give -- sorry. That should give the Defence counsels a reasonable time to prepare. And it also gives them the advantage of having heard the examination-in-chief and then have extra time, actually, between the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination. So in light of this advantage that the Defence teams get of not having to proceed immediately to the cross-examination, the Chamber thinks that this is a reasonable solution to -- to at least save some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention it's likely that the videolink witness will go into Wednesday. I anticipate that certainly one of my learned friends has got quite a lot to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, let's have your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can Your Honour just forgive me while I leave court for five minutes. Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Can the next witness Mirzet Karabeg be brought into court ready for his testimony, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, no protective measures apply to this witness; is that correct? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for coming to assist the Tribunal. Your name, sir, is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mirzet Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: This is -- your place of birth and date of birth, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born in Sanski Most, Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the 20th of December, 1943, in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. The procedure that will be followed this afternoon is the Prosecution, whose witness you are, will ask you questions for about 20 minutes, because this is an expedited hearing, after which the lawyers for the two accused would each have an opportunity to ask you questions for a slightly longer period of time. After that cross-examination, there may be re-examination by the counsel who has called you, and the Bench may have some questions, and when that is over, you would be released. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, in addition to the personal details you provided, you are also a Bosniak by ethnicity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You've testified here in a number of cases, and in particular I want to direct your attention to your testimony in the case against Brdjanin and General Talic, and you testified in that case, I believe, on the 27th of May, 28th, 29th, and 30th of May, 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And when you provided that testimony back then in 2002, did you endeavour to answer your questions as honestly and accurately as you could?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity of reviewing your testimony by the use of audio files or audio CDs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And if you were to be examined again on the same topics, asked the same questions again about the same topics, would you provide the same evidence to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, in accordance with the decision that you rendered on the 2nd of October, 2009, I'd like to seek the admission of the transcripts of his evidence together with a number of 65 ter exhibits. Do Your Honours want me to enumerate those 65 ter numbers now into the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The principle exhibit would be tendered and marked as usual, and you may leave it to the Registry system to indicate the sub-numbers as necessary. Of course, if in the course -- if it is necessary for you to identify a particular item from the subgroup, we devise a means for you to do that. But for the time being, it's sufficient for the transcript and its accompanying documents to be tendered and marked with the next number in the series. Mr. Pantelic, you have a difficulty?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't have difficulty, but I would just like to excuse myself for interrupting this line of questioning that my learned friend Mr. Di Fazio is just commencing. I would like to know, in terms of our future preparation, if that's true that this witness, Mr. Karabeg, testified in other cases than Mr. -- than Brdjanin, because if that's the case, we don't have any record or any documents or transcript from. So if my learned friend can clarify that. And if that's the case, I would instruct my associate to look for -- for these additional documents. MR. DI FAZIO: At least in the Krajisnik case. Just that. And that was in May 2004. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I'm given to understand that your concern may have been a reflection of the way that counsel's question came out. But, Mr. Di Fazio, the Prosecution is only -- is only relying on the transcript in Brdjanin. Isn't that the position? MR. DI FAZIO: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Pardon me? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I just mentioned that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel. MR. DI FAZIO: My microphone is not working. Can you hear me now? Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. The Prosecution's only using --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone is inactive again. MR. DI FAZIO: It appears to be switched on and red. It's also -- the red button is here, Your Honours. But I can hear myself, that my voice is not coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
